lines_of_inquiry.detail: The log's 'Viewpoints & Claims (plan)' lays out all five lines explicitly, each decomposed into numbered sub-claims: V1 asset-price channel (QE raises equity/bond/housing prices C1.1; asset ownership concentrated at top C1.2); V2 saver/borrower redistribution channel (net saver/debtor positions C2.1; HANK/Auclert heterogeneity C2.2); V3 macro employment/wage channel (does QE cut unemployment esp. for low earners C3.1; counterfactual unemployment path C3.2); V4 structural-force counterfactual baseline (pre-2008 top-1% wealth trend C4.1; decomposition of the rise into capital gains vs saving vs labor income C4.2); V5 the causal-identification problem itself (methods C5.1; their limits C5.2; whether a calibrated net verdict exists C5.3). The three channels flagged in the original question (A/B/C) map cleanly onto V1/V2/V3.

leanings.detail: A dedicated 'Claim conclusions' section gives a lean per claim: asset-price channel SUPPORTED (real, dis-equalizing, robust UK+US); ADV1 counterfactual MIXED (structural saving-glut/r* forces were already lifting valuations, weakening a maximalist 'QE caused it' read but not refuting an added boost); saver/borrower channel MIXED and second-order (sign depends on balance-sheet duration; income-flow effect an order of magnitude smaller than valuation effect); employment channel SUPPORTED as equalizing but 'swamped' by the equity channel; structural pre-existing trend SUPPORTED strongly (40-yr trend predates QE); identification SUPPORTED as a genuine hard problem. Root thesis stated in full: QE's causal contribution is REAL, CHANNEL-SPECIFIC and MODEST vs structural forces — net 'modestly dis-equalizing' for wealth-stock measures (per S8), with a wide, humble confidence band, and not explaining more than a fraction of the four-decade top-wealth-share rise.

key_figures.detail: Numerous specific figures with source tags survive: top 5% of UK households hold 40% of financial assets (S1); QE ~+16% household net-wealth boost / ~£600bn valuation effect vs ~£70bn lost deposit interest vs ~£100bn lower debt-service (S1); BIS decomposition — bonds negligible, equities dis-equalizing, housing equalizing/partly offsetting, top-1% share rising since the 1980s off 1810-2010 data (S4); Engen-Laubach-Reifschneider counterfactual peak unemployment effect of -1.25pp from unconventional policy (S7); Montecino-Epstein — employment + mortgage-refi equalizing (+~2.8pp to median) but swamped by equity appreciation (~-6pp on the 95/10 ratio), net 'modestly regressive' (S8); Fed DFA 2020-21 — revaluations ~80% of the $18tn wealth gain, yet Top-1% share up only 2.2pp and Bottom-50 up 0.2pp in the rebound (S9); Saez-Zucman — top-1% wealth-to-income ratio 60→200 years over 1980-2020 (S6).

adversarial_lines.detail: Four rival/counter explanations are stated in the plan AND resolved in the conclusions: ADV1 = valuations would have risen anyway via Mian-Straub-Sufi 'saving glut of the rich' pushing down r* since the 1980s (reverse causality — QE partly endogenous to the same inequality it is blamed for); ADV2 = the saver/borrower channel may actually help lower/middle net-debtors (mortgage holders), offsetting the asset channel; ADV3 = the employment channel helps bottom-income flows enough to offset — resolved by the explicit income-inequality vs wealth-inequality distinction (employment wins for income/wage flows, equity channel wins for wealth stocks); ADV4 = if the pre-2008 and 2008-2021 top-wealth-share slopes are indistinguishable, QE's marginal contribution is doubtful. ADV4 is the one line left OPEN — no formal structural-break-test study was found, flagged as a live uncertainty rather than a settled refutation.
